what_this_is: Oracle to PostgreSQL scalar type mapping, as data. NUMBER(p,0) is mapped to the smallest exact integer type that holds p digits, by the thresholds below; NUMBER(p,s) keeps its precision as NUMERIC(p,s); bare NUMBER stays NUMERIC. Anything in 'unmappable' has no safe mapping and routes the object to a person. Types owned by a system schema are never mapped.

NATURAL.note: the non-negative constraint is not carried

POSITIVE.note: the positive constraint is not carried

DATE.note: Oracle DATE carries time to the second; PostgreSQL DATE does not

XMLTYPE.note: XML type only; no schema validation on the target

unmappable.ROWID: no stable row address in PostgreSQL (ctid moves on update)
unmappable.UROWID: no stable row address in PostgreSQL
unmappable.ANYDATA: no equivalent; a decision, not a mapping
unmappable.BFILE: an external file locator has no equivalent
unmappable.SYS_REFCURSOR: refcursor exists but calling conventions differ; model tier
